description: Figure 4.1 presents a series of five line plots illustrating the Word Error Rate (WER) during the fine-tuning of the Whisper model across different configurations, each corresponding to a specific type of model size: tiny, base, small, medium, and large. The horizontal axis, labeled 'epoch', ranges from 0 to 6, representing the training epochs. The vertical axis, labeled 'WER', is scaled from 10 to 70, indicating the error rate. Each plot displays multiple lines, each representing a different variant of the model, such as 'tiny AdaLoRA_int4', 'tiny int4', 'tiny full', and so on, with distinct colors and line styles to differentiate them. The data points are plotted at each epoch, showing the WER value for each model variant. In the 'tiny' plot, all lines show a general downward trend, with the 'tiny full' model achieving the lowest WER. In the 'base' plot, the 'base full' model starts with the highest WER and ends with the lowest. The 'small' plot shows the 'small AdaLoRA_int8' model achieving the lowest WER. The 'medium' plot shows a similar trend, with the 'medium AdaLoRA_int8' model achieving the lowest WER. The 'large' plot shows the 'large AdaLoRA_int8' model achieving the lowest WER. The caption indicates that these plots compare the WER performance of the Whisper model when fine-tuned with different amounts of weights, highlighting the impact of model size and fine-tuning strategy on the final error rate.
